A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CP-OPT and CROQ and retain the same core experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on MMLU, TruthfulQA and ToolAlpaca, including accuracy, coverage, set sizes, distractor removal and deferral analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds MMLU-Pro and BIRD/NL2SQL evaluations, alongside a revised distractor-removal experiment.

M1.justification: Equation (2) changes the stated calibration rule from an empirical alpha quantile to a finite-sample threshold using floor((ncal+1)alpha). The CP-OPT objective, network and core CROQ steps remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun using the corrected rule.

E1.justification: V2 adds harder, 10-option MMLU-Pro questions and BIRD-based NL2SQL evaluation in Appendices C.2-C.3. The latter extends coverage from selecting individual MCQ answers or tools to selecting database schemas and evaluating generated SQL. All three original datasets remain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 introduces a cosine-similarity threshold selector, capped at 10 tables, alongside an all-schema control for comparison with CP-OPT. Figure 1 adds a random-choice reference curve. Comparator membership in the original benchmark experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The motivating experiment changes from removing 0-10 distractors from 95%-coverage conformal sets to removing up to 14 distractors from full questions, and adds Gemma-2. The new BIRD evaluation specifies filtering, 3,412 training, 3,411 validation and 200 test pairs, GPT4-0613, execution accuracy and token cost.

E4.justification: The controlled distractor-removal analysis is revised and expanded while testing the same underlying question (v1 Figure 2; v2 Figure 1). The NL2SQL case study additionally examines pruning's accuracy-cost tradeoff. Existing coverage sweeps, deferral analyses and results conditional on set size are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 1 newly reports averages across five iterations and error bars of plus or minus two standard deviations; v1's corresponding motivating figure reported neither. The paired t-tests at the 0.05 level and their appendix explanation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds a reported 3% relative CROQ improvement over a 36.4% Phi-3 baseline on MMLU-Pro. Its new BIRD Table 4 reports 32.5% accuracy and $3.89 cost for CP-OPT versus 32.0% and $7.10 for all schemas. Revised distractor curves use different conditions; original benchmark table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds a formal monotone-accuracy assumption and Proposition 3.2, covering an accuracy decomposition, a sufficient improvement condition and a greedy optimality claim. Appendix B adds proofs of this proposition and the coverage guarantee. Equation (2) also receives a substantive finite-sample correction.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that CP-OPT reduces conformal set sizes, CROQ improves MCQ accuracy, and CP-OPT can improve CROQ over logits. V2 reorders and separates these contributions without materially changing their scientific scope or the central novelty claim.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies its new analysis by acknowledging dependence between set-size frequencies, conditional coverage and conditional accuracy (Appendix B.2). It also interprets schema pruning as a way to reduce SQL-generation costs. Existing coverage-accuracy tradeoffs and multi-round calibration concerns largely persist.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds NL2SQL implementation information, including text-embedding-ada-002, GPT4-0613, embedding inputs and database filtering rules. The original network specification moves from the appendix into Section 3.2, while the original hyperparameters and training-budget disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes the Monty Hall references and adds citations for MMLU-Pro, BIRD, conformal nucleus sampling, the knapsack argument and additional coverage theory. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing conformal-score methods otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title to Prune 'n Predict, substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and conclusion, and presents CROQ before CP-OPT. It replaces the Monty Hall narrative with pruning-based motivation and reorganizes the appendices, moving coverage and deferral discussions out of the main text.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document-wide typography, text width, headers and table placement. It redraws the motivating plot, adds the NL2SQL table, and relocates several existing displays. Two Gemma-2 histogram groups visualize previously tabulated results, while a duplicated Phi-3 histogram is removed.

improvement.justification: The corrected calibration formula, explicit uncertainty in the motivating experiment, clearer organization and new practical evaluations provide a modest net improvement. Gains are limited by sparse MMLU-Pro documentation and a gap in Proposition 3.2: its claimed exact accuracy decomposition omits potentially correct empty-set fallback answers allowed by Step 2. The core benchmark evidence is unchanged.
